patients.label: Case: 67-year-old man with prior HIT and end-stage renal disease undergoing left atrial appendage occlusion with argatroban
attribution_limitations: The two HIT episodes are described with one shared time phrase and platelet nadirs paired by "respectively".

The case text says the team utilized percutaneous coronary intervention recommendations and that the literature calls for a 350 mcg/kg bolus and 25 mcg/kg/min infusion; these are literature recommendations, not doses given to this patient.

The discussion states this patient remained significantly anticoagulated postoperatively without giving a value or time; the case text gives an ACT of 370 s only at about 1 h after the infusion stopped.

Figure 1 plots ACT values over time; the plotted points and event arrows are pixel content recorded only in the visual target. Plotted x positions (e.g. the 262 s point and the infusion arrows) were not read numerically and need not match the approximate intervals stated in the text.

The discussion says the patient again rapidly became supratherapeutic after the infusion was started; the case sentence reporting the 526 s ACT does not itself call that value supratherapeutic, so its flag stays unknown.
Admission was to receive hemodialysis the next day; whether the hemodialysis was performed is not reported.

claims.text: A 67-year-old man with a past medical history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia type II, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease and end-stage renal disease on intermittent hemodialysis presented for left atrial appendage occlusion with the Watchman device. Six months earlier he had a non-ST segment elevation myocardial infarction while taking apixaban, which was subsequently discontinued after EGD findings. Procedure-day platelet count was 85,000 cells/mcL.
